channel-plan.note: silkscreen - channels alternate in pairs between rows, 921/922 top then 923/924 bottom, continuing to 960

column-grid.note: top and bottom rows agreed across all 23 columns, so one averaged grid is used and the drawing jitter discarded

markings.note: photo - IEC 60825 laser hazard triangles in the gap between the two port blocks, matching the 34D

mgmt-jack-alignment.note: stencil, correcting a transcription slip. The ShapeSheet puts ETH0 and RS232 within 0.14mm of the same x (fractions 0.0828 and 0.0831) and the art draws the shells flush, but the model had them 1.2mm apart at 9.6 and 10.8. ETH0 moved onto RS232's x, and its rotated caption with it. RS232 is the half that already matched, so it did not move

osc-captions.note: stencil art. As on the 34D, the Tx and Rx captions sat 4.3mm and 1.9mm from their own LEDs on opposite sides and threw the pair 1.65mm left of the cage. The LEDs were already right - measured at 34.98 and 40.81 against the model's 34.9 and 40.7, which is what validates this master's coordinate mapping to 0.1mm. Captions moved to 31.9 and 43.85

port-pairing.note: each LC duplex adapter carries two connection points about 6.6mm apart, one per fiber; adapters recovered by pairing those

port-positions.note: stencil ShapeSheet connection points, which Visio stores as fractions of shape width/height and therefore survive without the drawing scale. Resolved against the 19-inch rack width the master is drawn at. ADAPTER BODIES MOVED, FIBRES DID NOT (common/lc-duplex-adapter@6, B3): that adapter's ferrule axis sits 5.82 from its latch-side edge where @4's sat at 5.5, so every placement of it here moved 0.32 toward its own latch side - up on an unturned row, down on a row at rotate 180, with the panel cutout of the same id - and each fibre stays on the position read above.

port-speeds.note: the OSC cage is `1g`: the DCP-R user manual (14.0), Supported OSC transceivers, certifies SFPs from 155 Mb/s STM-1/Fast Ethernet parts up to 1GE ones, and its OTDR section offers the combined OSC/OTDR SFP at 155 Mb/s or 1 Gb/s. The highest native rate the cage runs at is therefore 1G.

psu-orientation.note: photo - both modules are fitted the same way round, fan inboard of the inlet, so the C14 sits at the far right on PSU-2 and inboard on PSU-1. They are not mirrored

psu-part.note: label - Gospower G1251-0550WNA, P/N CRPS0550-AH, and the fan sticker reads 550W Platinum CRPS. So the module is a standard CRPS 1U part at 73.5 x 40 x 185, not the 84mm-wide estimate taken from the racked photo, and both bays sit flush to the chassis edges

rear-layout.note: photo IMG_2181 of racked DCP-R units - PSU with integrated fan and C14 inlet at each end, mirrored; honeycomb vent panel across the centre; management block right of centre. Block positions are approximate to about 3mm - the photo has uncorrected perspective and partial cable occlusion, so it fixes the structure and order but not exact millimetres

rear-mgmt-block.note: stencil master dcp-r-rear, which is orthographic - a 2x2 ganged RJ45 shell (ETH 2 / ETH 4 over ETH 1 / ETH 3), ESD warning, Tx and Rx LEDs, an ETH 5 SFP cage and a recessed RESET button

side-top-bottom.note: IMG_2188 shows the lid, so these now carry the real finish - a light silver body with the black front panel wrapping about 12.7mm (half an inch) back along every face. Still no vents, screws or lid labels - the photo shows the finish and the panel depth but not those details, so they are left out rather than invented

status-leds.note: stencil art - Power and Status centres measured at 54.79 and 60.88, a 6.09mm pitch, against the 5.6 the model carried. Same defect and the same correction as the 34D, and the two masters agree on the pitch to 0.02mm

tx-rx-boxes.note: photo - every optical port carries a boxed Tx/Rx pair between its name and the adapter, split by a divider, reversed on the bottom row

tx-rx-drawn.note: THE TWO FIGURES THE MEASURED CENTRES ARE DRAWN WITH, neither read off a source. The FRAME HEIGHT is 2.5, a drawn size where the stencil's box is 1.7-1.8: only its centre is the stencil's (`tx-rx-positions`). The NAME BASELINES are placed from the measured glyph centre by taking the cap height as 0.72 of the font size - an assumed ratio, not a measured one - so a baseline is as good as that ratio, while the glyph centre it is derived from is measured

tx-rx-positions.note: THE CENTRES, MEASURED - and only the centres; the figures drawn around them are `tx-rx-drawn`. Stencil master r-9d-csx, read at 8.33 px/mm vertically - its two ferrule rows stand 92 px apart against this model's 11.05 row pitch, the same fit the 34D's 8.86 comes from, and within 1.7% of the 45/46.0 y-scale above - each figure measured outward from the art's own ferrule line and taken as the row's median, since this master is a JPEG and single pairs scatter by about 0.2. The white Tx/Rx box runs 7.68 to 9.38 from the ferrule on the top row and 7.65 to 9.45 on the bottom row; the port name's glyphs run 10.02 to 12.00 and 10.26 to 12.18. Each frame is centred on the box's centre, its divider and Tx/Rx text move with it, and each name's glyph is centred on the stencil name's centre. Until B3 the frames were generated from each adapter's placement 5.85 from the ferrule, about 1.8 closer than the stencil draws them, and once the adapter bodies moved to keep the fibres on the connection points (common/lc-duplex-adapter@6) the bodies met them. The boxed style is the photograph's (`tx-rx-boxes`); only the positions are the stencil's

xc-orientation.note: stencil master r-9d-csx - THE BOTTOM ROW IS MIRRORED, latch tongues down against the top row's up, exactly as on the 34D. The drawing already encoded it: every bottom-row port prints its Tx/Rx box reversed. It could not be DRAWN until std/lc-bore@3 made the bore keyed (#126), because a 4.7 square has no orientation. All 23 bottom-row adapters now carry rotate: 180

y-scale.note: this master is drawn 46.0mm tall against a 45mm chassis, so y was scaled by 45/46.0. The 34D master needed no such correction - a reminder that masters in one stencil are not all drawn to the same scale
